courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Music Appreciation
courses.description: Designed to increase awareness and appreciation of music from the European classical tradition in relation to general culture and history. Develops basic understanding of musical elements and deepens student's experience of music. Recommended for non-music majors. CSU/UC

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Honors Music Appreciation
courses.description: An enriched approach designed for honors students. The European classical music tradition through study of musical elements, stylistic features, culture, and history. Readings, guided listening assignments, required concert attendance, and special projects. Recommended for non-music majors. CSU/UC

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: World Music
courses.description: Music from the Far East, Southeast Asia, Africa, the Middle East, Europe and the Americas. Students are guided to enjoy and to understand music from diverse cultures. Investigation of the interconnections of culture, aesthetics, and musical styles. Concert attendance and assigned listening required. CSU/UC

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Honors World Music
courses.description: An enriched, in-depth study of music from Asia, Africa, the Middle East, Europe, and the Americas. Seminar-style critical investigation of the interconnections of style, culture, and aesthetics to promote enjoyment and understanding of world music. CSU/UC

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Rock Music History and Appreciation
courses.description: Historical survey of rock music from its beginnings in the 50's to the present. Major rock and pop styles will be discussed. Personalities and musical styles will be related to the social, political, and cultural context of the time. CSU/UC

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Reading and Making Music
courses.description: Introduction to music reading. Practical experience in learning how to perform melodies, rhythms, and simple chords from a written score. Recommended for beginning instrumental and voice students and those preparing for music theory. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Music Fundamentals
courses.description: An introduction to the notation and fundamental theoretical elements of Western music, demonstrated through a variety of styles, covering: pitch and rhythm concepts and structures, basic formal elements, and fundamental musicianship. Development of skills in handwritten notation is expected. In addition, interpreting music, written and aurally, with regard to its broad historical and cultural context will be covered, and critiquing different musical genres and styles in order to make aesthetic judgments about them by applying criteria from the knowledge and principles of music theory learned in class. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Music Theory and Musicianship I
courses.description: Introductory level course in music theory and its applications in traditional and modern musical practice. Includes detailed study of rhythm, notation, scales, intervals, chords, diatonic harmony, and voice leading as well as sight singing and other musicianship skills. Ability to read music in at least one clef recommended. Required of music majors; open to non-majors. CSU/UC

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Musicianship Skills
courses.description: Continued ear training and in-class sight-singing preparation for students not ready for Music 114A. Arranged hours in Music Lab for computer programs and ear training programs. Basic knowledge of scales and intervals recommended. Grade: Pass/No Pass Only. A combination of Music 113A, 113B, 114A, and 114B may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC

notes: CU0002 is parsed explicitly; unrecognized catalog layouts are not guessed.
Crosswalk ownership is college-aware; ambiguous ownership remains flagged instead of silently assigned.
CU0321 last-offered data is a planning signal only and does not determine curriculum currency.
DO NOT SCHEDULE rooms are owner-only when a matching owner division is present; they are not campuswide rooms.
Shared portal writes are revalidated server-side; browser-calculated totals are not trusted.
Local database mode writes proposals to SQLite with revision history and stores per-department draft workspaces; static HTML is preview-only for database actions.
Department draft workspaces are isolated by term/college/division/department so switching scope does not destroy unfinished work.
2026-27 credit default is Standardized Attendance Accounting; open-entry/open-exit credit remains Actual Hours / Positive Attendance.
Faculty load caps/factors are configurable planning values, not a contractual certification.
Pathway membership comes only from a confirmed administrator-provided mapping; it is never inferred from course title, TOP code, or division.
Imported existing bookings are a snapshot at generation time, not a live Ad Astra/Colleague connection; regenerate after refreshing the booking export.
Empty optional booking/pathway CSV files are ignored with import warnings; malformed or headerless files produce a clear validation error instead of a raw csv traceback.
RG0547 prepopulation maps prior dates by relative term week + weekday; previous CRNs are retained only as a reference and are never reused as current-term identifiers.
Block schedule alignment is advisory. The planner suggests approved windows and permits documented exceptions rather than blocking CTE/long-format schedules.
Department-chair modality labels are translated to scheduler/Colleague codes from the imported DE coding reference when available.
